title: One-Pot Creamy Pea & Potato Soup
description: Potatoes and frozen peas simmer into a simple creamy soup made with ordinary refrigerator and freezer staples.
substitutions: Use evaporated milk for a richer soup.
Use frozen mixed vegetables instead of peas.
Stir in shredded cheddar at the end if desired.

steps.text: Mash some of the potatoes and add peas and milk.

cookSteps.text: Put 1 1/2 pounds diced potatoes, 3 cups broth, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper in a large saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer.
Cover loosely and simmer for 18 minutes, until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash about half of the potatoes right in the pot. Stir in 1 1/2 cups frozen peas, 1 cup milk, and 1 tablespoon butter.
Cook gently for 5–7 minutes, stirring often, until the peas are hot and the soup is creamy. Do not let the milk boil hard.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of milk if the soup thickens.

title: Turkey & Spinach Tortilla Melts
description: Deli turkey, spinach, and melted cheese turn tortillas into a fast lunch or light dinner with almost no prep.
substitutions: Use deli ham instead of turkey.
Use chopped cabbage or leftover cooked vegetables instead of spinach.
Add mustard inside the tortillas if desired.

steps.text: Toast both sides until crisp and melted.

cookSteps.text: Divide 4 ounces deli turkey, 1 cup baby spinach, and 1 cup shredded cheese over one half of each of 2 large tortillas. Fold the tortillas closed.
Heat 1 teaspoon butter or oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the folded tortillas for 4–5 minutes on the first side, pressing lightly, until golden.
Flip and cook 3–4 minutes more, until the second side is golden and the cheese is melted. Cut into wedges and serve.

storage: Best eaten fresh. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days and reheat in a dry skillet.

title: Leftover Vegetable & Cheesy Rice Soup
description: Leftover cooked rice and vegetables become a cozy, lightly cheesy soup instead of another container forgotten in the refrigerator.
substitutions: Use leftover pasta instead of rice.
Use any mild melting cheese instead of cheddar.
Add leftover beans for a heartier soup.

steps.text: Heat the rice, vegetables, broth, and seasoning.
Finish gently with milk and cheese.

cookSteps.text: Combine 2 cups leftover cooked rice, 2 cups chopped leftover cooked vegetables, 4 cups broth, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper in a large saucepan.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything is steaming hot.
Reduce the heat to low. Stir in 1/2 cup milk and 3/4 cup shredded cheddar. Cook for 3–5 minutes, stirring, just until the cheese melts. Do not boil hard.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat gently with extra broth or milk as needed.

title: Small-Batch Cinnamon Pear Bread Pudding
description: Stale bread and one ripe pear bake into a soft cinnamon custard dessert sized for a small household.
substitutions: Use a small apple instead of the pear.
Use white sugar if brown sugar is unavailable.
Use slightly less sugar if the pear is very sweet.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a small baking dish. Put 3 cups stale bread cubes and 1 diced ripe pear in the dish.

Whisk 1 egg, 1 cup milk, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 tablespoon melted butter, 3/4 teaspoon cinnamon, and 1/4 teaspoon vanilla if using. Pour over the bread and pear, press gently so the bread absorbs the custard, and let stand 5 minutes.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the center is set and the top is lightly browned. Serve warm.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat individual portions gently in the microwave or oven.
